item.research_question: How does a novel refractory high entropy alloy (NV1) behave under long-term isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C and 1100 °C, and what is the mechanism governing its oxidation resistance over 200 hours?
item.material_system: NV1 alloy (Al, Cr, Mo, Nb, Si, Ta, Ti; designed based on CrMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr with reduced Ti, removed Zr, and added Al, Si, increased Cr)
item.processing_route: Cold crucible levitation melting of high purity elemental raw materials (>99.9 wt%) to cast a 1.1 kg cone-shaped ingot; samples machined by electrical discharge machining and ground to 1200 grit; isothermal oxidation performed in flowing dry air using a thermogravimetric analyser (SETARAM TAG 24-18S) and muffle furnace
item.test_conditions: Isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C and 1100 °C for up to 200 hours in flowing dry air; microstructural characterization performed at intervals of 1, 12, 40, 50, 100, and 200 hours
key_findings: At 1000 °C, the mass gain after 200 hours was 6.53 mg/cm2, following an exponential dependence throughout the entire duration.
At 1100 °C, the mass gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm2, which is lower than at 1000 °C, showing three stages of parabolic dependence.
The external oxide layer at both temperatures consisted primarily of a CrTaO4-based oxide with dispersed Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
At 1000 °C, the CrTaO4-based oxide layer was porous with large volume defects due to insufficient kinetics, preventing it from acting as an effective barrier.
At 1100 °C, the CrTaO4-based oxide layer was denser and more continuous, leading to controlled oxidation and reduced weight gain.
TiN particles (size ~1.5 μm) formed preferentially within the Mo-rich dendritic regions at both temperatures, while Al2O3 formed in the internal oxidation depth.
The CrTaO4-based oxide at 1100 °C contained up to 7 at% Al and 2.2 at% less Cr compared to the oxide formed at 1000 °C, indicating non-stoichiometric substitution.
item.mechanism: At 1000 °C, insufficient kinetics prevented the formation of a dense, protective CrTaO4 layer, leading to heterogeneous oxidation, volume defects, and exponential weight gain driven by external oxidation and nitridation. At 1100 °C, enhanced diffusion kinetics allowed for the homogeneous growth of a denser, continuous CrTaO4-based layer that acted as a barrier to oxygen and element diffusion, resulting in parabolic weight gain; however, Mo evaporation at the oxide/substrate interface in Stage II temporarily accelerated oxidation before Stage III saw further CrTaO4 formation.
item.limitations: The study notes that while CrTaO4-based oxide provided protection, it could not fully prevent the ingestion of oxygen and nitrogen, leading to internal oxidation and nitridation over the long duration.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the nature of the CrTaO4-based oxide needs to be carefully examined in future studies, and that the influence of nitridation on RHEA properties is an important subject for further investigation.
quotes: At 1100 °C, mass gain curve showed two parabolic dependences associated with the formation of protective CrTaO4-based oxide layer and the weight gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm2
At 1000 °C, the inability to form dense CrTaO4-based oxide layer resulted an exponential dependence of weight gain throughout 200 hours.
The CrTaO4-based oxide layer observed in present study showed different lattice constants and compositions at 1000 and 1100 °C.
